mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during an expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero during triggered periods, or the effect is absent during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, accompanied by a concurrent rise in the producer price index (CPIAUCSL), signals an inflationary supply shock that erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA for 2 months AND CPIAUCSL > previous 12-month average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of falling input costs.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 alongside a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and increases recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumer spending intentions, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods, or the effect is absent in high-inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.75 percentage points within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent outside crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA AND HOUST < 12-month MA for the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during supply-chain normalization.
